note_tweet.text:
there could be no better time to launch muse spark 1.

comparing to the recent grok 4.5 release, it performs on a similar level to opus 4.8 and gpt 5.5, except has a large 1m context window compared to grok 4.5s 200k context window

they also wins on pricing per performance, as it's $1.25/m in, $0.15 cache in, and $4.25 out. this surely beats grok 4.5 ($2/m in and $6/m out) which was already cheaper than a bunch of the models it was comparing to

cool side bonus is that they focused also on computer use which seems to be growing heavily in popularity especially for some coding based tasks

this seems to follow a general trend that labs attempting to catch up to the frontier status are working on aggressive pricing, pulling model costs down which is always a huge win for the community 

if your interested in testing it out they have a new api to access it plus $20 in free credits

note_tweet.text:
wtf. How did Meta just drop Muse Spark 1.1 that actually rivals GPT-5.5 and Opus 4.8 on agentic evals??

Leaps from previous Muse Spark:
• JobBench (prof tool use): 17 → 54.7 (+222%)
• OSWorld computer use: 53.3 → 80.8
• DeepSWE long-horizon coding: 10 → 53.3 (+433%)
• BabyVision visual reasoning: 39.9 → 76.3

1M context + real computer use (script or click) + public API at decent pricing. 

The agentic leap is insane. How are they moving this fast?
